title: introduce-policy-drift-detector-installer-kms-affinity-and-audit-enrichment
author: Marina Soloviev
description: Motivation: in private deployments we observed subtle RBAC v2 policy regressions during iterative operator changes, and mismatches between declared KMS residency expectations and the installer-provisioned keys. This PR adds three coordinated features to reduce operational risk: 1) a policy-drift detector that runs as part of the installer CI and periodically as a cron job in the private control plane; it snapshots effective RBAC role graphs and compares against a committed policy baseline using a compact 'diff' algorithm tuned for large role graphs so we surface meaningful drift rather than noisy ordering changes; 2) a KMS affinity preflight hook in the installer that validates tenant-declared region pinning against available CMKs and tags keys with a residency provenance tag (kms.residency) when creating or binding keys; and 3) an audit enrichment pipeline that appends normalized residency and provenance headers to audit events and emits an integrity-proof hash to make post-hoc audits and reconciliations easier. Summary of changes: added a new installer hook package (installer/hooks/policy_drift_detector.go) with an OPA-based rule set that performs semantic comparisons and a small runner for baseline snapshots; added an installer KMS adapter (installer/hooks/kms_affinity_check.go) that performs cloud-provider key lookups and writes provenance tags; added an audit enricher service (installer/audit/enricher/enricher.go) that normalizes residency headers and computes a per-event HMAC for tamper-evidence; added integration e2e definitions (installer/ci/policy-e2e.yaml) and docs (docs/upgrade/2026-02-policy-drift.md); updated the installer CLI to expose --enforce-kms-affinity and --drift-detector-schedule flags; added tests and benchmarks. Rollout and compatibility: all features are opt-in for upgrades; the installer defaults keep previous behavior unless --enforce-kms-affinity is set. The drift detector can be enabled in a staged rollout using the existing canary mechanism; the audit enricher runs when audit-forwarding is enabled. Migration notes: a migration task is included that takes a one-time snapshot of current role bindings and stores it under installer/state/baseline-v1.json; this snapshot is used as the reference for the first run and can be regenerated. Security review: KMS calls are limited to explicit operator-scoped credentials, provenance HMAC keys are stored only in customer-provided CMKs when running in Private mode, and OPA rule execution is sandboxed. Testing: unit tests for rules, integration tests against the private-installer mock provider, and a full e2e run against a small multi-tenant cluster were executed as part of the CI. Related work: follows up on SEC-78 and complements ENG-2026 policy linter efforts. Next steps: add a telemetry metric for 'drift_violation_rate' to Redwood Console and wire an alerting rule for recurring drift across more than 2 snapshots.
